messages:
liam: FYI scheduling a soft drain + rolling reboots for pool-us-east1-gpu-preemptive next Tue 03/31 02:00-05:00 UTC. Targeting BMC + NIC microcode updates across 6 racks. No full-region outage expected but pods will be evicted briefly.

maya: what's the planned capacity/backfill approach? last time we saw token spikes during backfill.

liam: good call — plan is staggered cordon -> drain per-rack, backfill from eu pool and local warm spares. We'll keep 10% headroom until caches are warmed. Goal: keep p95 latency within SLA.

jordan: can we prewarm ephemeral nodes instead of overprovisioning for the entire window? cheaper if we only need short bursts.

liam: yes. prewarm strategy: spin up N warmers with `--no-evict` worker profile, run a quick kv-cache-warm job, then flip traffic with our router policy. If warmers hit desired hit-rate we deprovision extra capacity.

sam: add a safety: if backfill hit CPU/GPU memory > 90% for >3m abort and fallback to reduced concurrency. we should script rollback.

liam: agreed. abort rule: if p95 latency > 2x baseline OR GPU mem pressure > 92% OR node drain failures > 3 in a row -> stop and escalate.

jordan: putting together a snippet for cordon/drain to use in runbook:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
NODE_LABEL=$1 # e.g. rack=us-east1-rack7
kubectl get nodes -l $NODE_LABEL -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl cordon
kubectl get pods -l pool=gpu-preemptive -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.nodeName!=null) | .metadata.name' | xargs -r -n1 kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

tanya: CS: please add the customer notification template. We have two customers running multi-hour evals in that region — want to give them 48h notice and an opt-out window.

liam: will do. I'll draft notice and post in #customer-notify and ping you for approval.

infra-bot: calendar event created: "us-east1 soft drain - BMC/NIC update" Tue 2026-03-31 02:00-05:00 UTC. Invitees: eng-infra, eng-sre, oncall. Link: https://calendar.example/evt/3854123456

deploy-bot: preflight check triggered by liam. Status: queued. Checks: image-compat, kv-cache-health, ingress-health.

maya: can we run a cost check? prewarm + short burst vs full reserved backfill — want an estimate of token/GPU-hour delta.

liam: quick calc: prewarm (6 warm nodes * 3h) ~18 node-hours. Overprovisioning whole window (20 spare nodes * 3h) ~60 node-hours. At current spot rates prewarm is ~70% cheaper for this window. I'll attach numbers to the incident doc.

sam: ops checklist draft (short):
- announce 48h to customers
- create calendar + pager schedule
- preflight run (deploy-bot)
- spin warmers + kv-warm job
- cordon/drain per rack (max parallel 2 racks)
- monitor p95 latency, GPU mem, node drain errors
- if abort -> restore traffic and escalate to oncall

liam: will run a dry run Fri 03/28 02:00 UTC on a small cohort (rack7) to validate. low-risk, no customer notice for dry run.

tanya: thanks — CS will prepare messaging and list of active long-jobs.

oncall: acked. I'll be on rotation for the window.

jordan: I'll own the warmers + routing flip scripts. putting PR up today for runbook updates.

liam: perfect. tagging action owners: @jordan (warmers), @sam (abort rules + monitoring), @tanya (customer notices). We'll reconvene Mon 03/30 16:00 UTC for final go/no-go. :thumbsup:

sam: noted. I'll add Grafana panels for quick scroll: p95 latency, GPU mem pct, drain-fail-count.

liam: thank you — closing thread for now, will post final runbook + customer notices here when ready.
